subject: q10jc built: reap = proc_find only (sha 743e5eda, spare 4096)
body: Image gpu/build/device-mmu-q10jc-candidate/ui-sched/nord2-ios-metal-q10jc-ui654fb60dvfs-cap3500-ram3776-sched.img sha256 743e5eda732a5a3f6cb315808e590829aaef48fc11e68aef42e9113e7980db31, 33550336 B, spare 4096, FAILURES none, kernel e7b8c69d, 0310 b8063a87. n2vr_reap: dead = (proc_find(pid) == NULL); proc_uniqueid/proc_exiting removed there (object no longer references _proc_exiting); r11 has no wait; all other breadcrumbs as q10jb. Header question: both are real exported kernel functions in the linked kernel (proc_exiting = ldr [x0,#0x460] bit 3; proc_uniqueid = p_proc_ro at +0x18, zone_require_ro, ro->p_uniqueid), not inlines from a mismatched proc_internal.h; and proc_uniqueid(p) already ran successfully in the probe's open (n2vr_by_proc, r3->r5 and the slot fill). So they are unlikely culprits on their own. CAVEAT for reading vc7: r11 came ~300 ms after r10 while the probe's open was in its 0.5 s exit wait after '=0'; the next line (r12) was due about when the probe's d_open returned to the kernel's open path. vc6b ended the same way (death ~0.5 s after the open's '=0'). The deaths therefore fit 'right after the relay d_open returns' as well as 'in the reap after r11'. If q10jc dies again, read: r12 present -> not the uniqueid/exiting calls; none of the probe's i1/r20 lines -> the open-return path.
